Thanks again for a productive call this morning. Recap of what we heard and proposed next steps below so we stay aligned on scope and success criteria.

Quick recap of SLOs you called out:
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 150ms for 1.5k token streaming responses (customer-facing chat)
- Throughput: sustained 200 RPS at peak (30-minute windows)
- Concurrency: support 50 concurrent active user streams with graceful backpressure
- Streaming: partial-token streaming for first-byte < 60ms and then steady token emission

Primary constraints: budget target ~ $0.02 per active session tokenset (ballpark), and data residency in us-east.

Proposed next steps (owners & timeline):
1) Technical feasibility runbook — Rishi will produce an initial run showing config options (batching, cache, quantization, model variants) and expected unit economics — due Thu EOD (2027-08-05).

Thanks Marissa — quick technical notes from my side to frame the pilot configuration and the tradeoffs we'll present on Friday. I kept this high-level so we can iterate after we see Priya's traces.

1) Model variants
- Candidate models: redwood-3b (fast, low-cost), redwood-xl (balanced), vicuna-13b (higher quality, higher compute).
- Pilot approach: test redwood-xl quantized + vicuna-13b 8-bit as a fallback for higher-quality sessions.

2) Quantization profiles
- 8-bit quantization (int8) on redwood-xl gives ~1.6x throughput improvement vs fp16 with minor quality delta on chat tasks; 4-bit (nf4/int4) could reduce cost further but increases tail-latency variance and may impact some open-domain answers.

3) Continuous batching & adaptive batch sizing
- For stable 200 RPS we can use continuous batching with a 5-15ms batching window to group requests; effective throughput gains while keeping p95 within target. We should tune by observed inter-arrival times from Priya's sample.

4) Caching / prefix KV cache
- Many of your sessions have repeated prefixes (product IDs, onboarding prompts). Prefix/KV caching for warm sessions can cut effective compute by 20-40% for short-turn conversations.

5) Streaming tuning
- To meet first-byte <60ms (for streaming), we recommend a small hot-path model (redwood-3b quantized) to produce initial tokens while the larger model continues in parallel (fan-out strategy). This hybrid reduces perceived latency but adds orchestration complexity.

6) Autoscaling & graceful degradation
- Recommend pre-warming dedicated capacity for predicted peak windows and fallback to a cheaper model variant when concurrency passes 50. Include rate-limiter-based shedding for non-critical requests.

Cost/Unit math (ballpark)
- Baseline (redwood-xl fp16): $0.045 per 1k tokens
- redwood-xl int8: ~$0.028 per 1k tokens
- vicuna-13b-8bit (fallback): ~$0.06 per 1k tokens
- With 30% caching + batching gains, effective cost could approach your $0.02 target for many sessions. Full modeling attached.

I'll prepare the cost modeling spreadsheet and a short config matrix (batch size, window, quantization, model) and attach latency_samples.csv + redwood-cost-modeling.xlsx to the follow-up.

Action items I own: deliver detailed config matrix + cost modeling by Thu EOD (2027-08-05).
